name: Unclean Animals
overview: Scripture clearly distinguishes between clean and unclean animals, commanding God's people to separate themselves from what He has declared unclean, as seen in commands to differentiate clean beasts from unclean and to avoid making their souls abominable through contact with unclean creatures (Leviticus 20:25). The eating of unclean animals is prohibited and carries serious spiritual consequences, including being cut off from the people of God (Leviticus 7:21; Deuteronomy 14:3). This holiness principle is exemplified in the account of Noah, who took clean animals by sevens and unclean by twos into the ark (Genesis 7:2), and in prophetic warnings against those who defile themselves by consuming forbidden creatures like swine and mice (Isaiah 66:17). These instructions underscore God's call for His people to live distinctively, honoring Him through obedience to His dietary laws.
